entities.name: Rhahzadh
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Rhahzadh, originally Roch Vehan and known in Byzantine sources as Rhazates, was a Sasanian general of Armenian origin whose strategic command during the climactic phase of the Byzantine-Sasanian War of 602–628 profoundly impacted the destiny of both empires. His leadership culminated in the decisive Battle of Nineveh in December 627, a confrontation that directly led to the collapse of Sasanian military power and precipitated a period of severe internal instability within Persia. Rhahzadh's actions, though ultimately unsuccessful, represent a critical pivot point in Late Antique history, marking the end of a protracted conflict that exhausted two of the ancient world's most formidable powers just before the rise of Islam.

Promoted to the position of Spahbed (commander-in-chief) of the Sasanian forces in Mesopotamia by Shah Khosrow II, Rhahzadh was tasked with repelling the invading Byzantine army led by Emperor Heraclius. In the autumn of 627, as Heraclius advanced deep into Sasanian territory, Rhahzadh shadowed his movements, aiming to intercept the Byzantine forces before they could reach the capital, Ctesiphon. On December 12, 627, near the ruins of ancient Nineveh, Rhahzadh engaged Heraclius's army. Despite his tactical prowess, including a personal duel with Heraclius, Rhahzadh's forces were decisively defeated, and he himself was killed in the battle, reportedly by Heraclius himself. The Sasanian army suffered immense casualties, estimated at over 20,000 men.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Rhahzadh's command and ultimate defeat at the Battle of Nineveh in 627 CE critically weakened the Sasanian Empire, directly contributing to its internal collapse and paving the way for the Islamic conquests that reshaped the entire Near East.
